summary: C-J1 (FS-GG/.github#4710) binds the Coordination managed-group owner, pinned at (FS-GG/FS.GG.Coordination, ac22206560f3eddfea524ce8f752ff1d0dfeec4e, eng/managed_group_owner.py, sha256 d846dbe1..., 45315 bytes), into the inline caller of the fable-reference-public.yml job wasm-installed-c. The caller fetches the owner through its closed acquisition path, checks size and SHA-256 before import, then checks the contract and the owner's self-hash. It probes containment before provisioning and qualifies actual tool versions under the setup deadline. Every call is one require-empty run under one never-renewed phase deadline, with a fresh out_dir under the job root. Executables are identity-bound with a recorded basis, and the hashes of declared script inputs (validator, checker) are retained per group. The job's Python runs in a sudo systemd-run delegated unit with TasksMax/MemoryMax hard limits. Installed C is wired per invocation. The shell checker's --mode wasm prepares only the downloaded source and production graph and runs no browser. The caller's installed_c runs that checker as one group, then each family's Playwright --list and test invocation as its own group, and applies the 9-case list and result assertions per family. The browser host validator is content-addressed, so its hash is in the profile argv. Lessons: the supplier refuses control characters in argv; a test should validate every real call site against the real validate_profile at run time; cwd must lie inside the profile root; and a nested owner inside a leaf cannot work (the root would not be exclusive), so Playwright must be launched from the top-level owner. The WASM receiver targets published Workspace.Template 0.19.2 (archive ef5c5c2f..., source and peeled tag d15f085f, descriptor e8dbf895...), verified locally by publication check, signatures, scaffolds and receiver check. Still held: both steps (if: false), main() (RUNTIME_ADMITTED=False) and custody_gate before installed C; installed-c.json records failed with its first cause. The custody pilot (runs 39828121993, 39837319401 and 39845591542; record templates/wasm-custody-pilot-run-39845591542) has since established, on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (WebKit with recorded host packages) clean stock shutdown under require-empty, deadline retirement, owner survivor retirement and the Chromium support join; its pilot entry is now closed (PILOT_ADMISSION=None). Installed C has a held, separately admitted dispatch entry: .github/workflows/wasm-installed-c.yml job installed-c, whose first step refuses before any host write unless source carries the admission, and admitted_installed_sequence. While the literal INSTALLED_ADMISSION = None, that entry refuses before any acquisition. Once an admission PR sets it to the exact comment URL, the entry runs in order: validate the dispatch (main, admitted_ref = SHA = WORKFLOW_SHA = head, exact URL, attempt 1, unit, host evidence); load the owner and probe; require the unit read-back to match (TasksMax=6144, MemoryMax=12G, RuntimeMaxUSec=40min); require the recorded WebKit packages to be installed with no apt or dpkg process left (the step is byte-identical to the pilot's); run prepare_inputs and qualify_tools; open custody_gate(admitted=True) for itself only; run installed_c (27 cases) under INSTALLED_BUDGET (setup 840 s, installed 1230 s); collect evidence capped at 150 MiB. hosted_sequence, main() (RUNTIME_ADMITTED=False) and both literal-false steps stay closed and are not the lift path. One run is enforced by the admission plan (dispatch once, then a reset PR sets the constant back to None). Not established: the 27-case journey itself; most of prepare_inputs beyond the browsers, qualify_tools and the checker source stage have never run hosted; provenance of installer-output and host images; plus the pilot's recorded gaps (liveness at the deadline, per-browser argv, one WebKit build and package set, an orphaned browser).
title: Installed-WASM caller binds fsgg.managed-group-contract/1 and holds a separately admitted 0.19.2 dispatch entry
